AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: A retrospective study was conducted to clarify the risk factors of postoperative sacroiliac joint pain (SIJP) for posterior open lumbar surgery.

AbstractText.Label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: A total of 472 patients who underwent posterior lumbar surgery between January 2011 and December 2014 were included in this analysis. We recorded basic characteristics, surgical characteristics and SIJP information of each patient.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The incidence of postoperative SIJP is 13.8% in our study. Comparison of the incidence of SIJP between discectomy and PLIF indicated that SIJP incidence tended to be higher in PLIF patients. (p=0.029). Comparing with single segment group, SIJP occurred more frequently in multiple operative segments group. (p=0.025). Comparing the incidence of SIJP among different types of lumbar diseases, SIJP incidence is higher in lumbar stenosis group significantly. (p=0035).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Lumbar fusion surgery and multiple operative segments are interdependent risk factors for the postoperative SIJP. The incidence of postoperative SIJP also increases in patients with lumbar stenosis compared with lumbar disc herniation and lumbar spondylolisthesis.
